provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: 1962 reads `Omnipotens sempiterne` where 1862 reads `SMnipotens sempit6rne`; 1962 reads `dispositione mirabili` where 1862 reads `dispositi6ne mirdi`; 1962 reads `fortia` where 1862 reads `f6rtia`; 1962 reads `Confessoris` where 1862 reads `Confess6ris`; 1962 reads `precibus,` where 1862 reads `pr6cibus,`; 1962 reads `gloriam` where 1862 reads `gl6riam`; 1962 reads `Dominum.` where 1862 reads `Domiuum nostrum.`; 1862 sets no comma after the second ut; 1862 spells coelis where the 1962 spells caelis; 1862 conclusion is `Per Dominum nostrum.`; the 1962 prints the abbreviated cue only; 1862 layer damage: the ornamental initial, `mirdi` for `mirabili`, `Domiuum`; three automatic repairs to the 1962 text were reverted because the 1862 and the Mame both support the layer's reading. Corroboration: 1922 Mame, printed p. 756, artifact PDF p. 870, text layer: it prints the same Collect and the same conclusion cue as the 1962. Recorded limitation: Both books send the Mass to the same Common of a Confessor not a Bishop, second Mass (1862 [23], 1962 [25]) and print the same single proper Collect. The conclusion is the one place in this lane where the target prints an abbreviation the layer could not render, and it was read on the page. || REPAIRED by lane repair-1: re-read on the 300 dpi page image of artifact PDF p. 798, whose own printed folio 717 and running head Festa novembris (11, 12, 13) are legible at the head of the page, with the marginal marker P 4093 beside the oration, and the conclusion re-read again on a 3x crop. NO WORD NEEDED REPAIR. ONE TOKEN IS NOT A LETTER-FOR-LETTER PAGE READING and a reviewer must know it: the page prints the last word of the conclusion as a scribal abbreviation with a tilde over the n, and the stored string carries its ordinary expansion, as the earlier lane recorded. The abbreviation was read on the image and is not in doubt; only its expansion is editorial, and the LENGTH of the printed cue is unchanged. Every other token and all pointing were verified against the image.

propers.name: Collect
propers.text:
Omnipotens sempiterne Deus, qui dispositione mirabili infirma mundi eligis,
ut fortia quaeque confundas: concede propitius humilitati nostrae; ut, piis
beati Didaci Confessoris tui precibus, ad perennem in caelis gloriam
sublimari mereamur. Per Dominum.
